prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Production asset sheet for the Granite Cave in Pokémon Emerald reimagined as an intricate hand-cut PAPER theatre inside a pop-up ball. Transparent RGBA landscape canvas 1536x1024. Twelve COMPLETE separate cutout objects arranged in a strict 4 columns by 3 rows grid with generous transparent gaps and margins. No text, labels, grid, backdrop, ball shell or characters.
Style: distinctly FLAT stacked colored cardstock silhouettes, warm cream cut edges, visible paper fibers, small hand-folded creases, delicately drawn geological lines. Layering creates depth. No realistic cave render, no polygonal 3D model, no black rectangular backdrops. Warm slate-grey, muted taupe, moss green, restrained blue-grey shadow layers; lichen, little ferns, chipped edges and sediment stripes for rich intentional detail. Front-view cutouts, no orthographic floor tile.
Row1: (1) a tall irregular left cave wall from overlapping flat jagged grey paper rock sheets, scattered pale sediment bands, fern crevices, a sloped broken lower ledge; (2) a tall DIFFERENT right cave wall with stratified flat slate layers, small moss patches and a winding flat paper ladder fixed to one side, complete irregular outer edge; (3) one large asymmetrical open cave-mouth rim silhouette, irregular polygonal layered slate lip around a FULLY TRANSPARENT opening, not a symmetrical round architectural arch, thin flat paper; (4) a smaller deeper cave-mouth rim silhouette in darker blue-grey layered paper with FULLY TRANSPARENT opening, very different shape.
Row2: (1) a small flat dark charcoal jagged rock face that can sit far behind the two open rims, visible overlapping dark paper strata, irregular complete perimeter; (2) five separate individual thin layered paper stalactites of differing lengths arranged horizontally with transparent gaps, NO connecting ceiling bar; (3) three separate small layered paper stalagmites on a shared irregular low ground lip with some moss; (4) loose low stack of weathered slabs and a small fallen paper ladder, some grass and pale lichen.
Row3: (1) clump of mossy layered paper boulders with delicate fern leaves; (2) small flat paper fern with a pair of mushrooms and three individual folded leaves; (3) four separate loose grey paper pebbles, all complete, irregular oval/angular outlines, several paper layers and subtle drawn cracks, no common base; (4) low mineral seam of dull grey-blue quartz slivers and pale sediment layers, no glow, detailed paper craft.
Avoid repeated cloned objects; make each silhouette distinct. The result must look handmade and foldable, not like a photo of rocks pasted onto a sprite sheet. Preserve alpha transparency around and inside all open shapes.
alpha: Original RGBA copied unchanged; geometry selects each card.
